title: introduce-cost-refinery-microbatch-lane-slimmer-and-quant-slab-autocalibrator
author: Sana Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Customers with mid-sized tenant fleets reported uneven unit economics across SKUs despite using the same model versions. We observed hot tenants driving microburst traffic that made fixed microbatch defaults suboptimal — increasing per-token cost or violating latency SLOs during spikes. This PR adds the "Cost Refinery": a lightweight runtime component that (1) profiles short-term shape distributions, (2) suggests microbatch lane shapes, and (3) autocalibrates per-tenant quantization slabs when safe. The goal is to reduce token cost without impacting tail latency or degrading model output quality.

What this PR does (high level):
- New runtime component: cost_refinery service that runs inside the shard-manager and exposes a local gRPC endpoint for policy suggestion. It samples request shapes and KV cache hit ratios and computes candidate microbatch lanes.
- Microbatch lane slimmer: a scoring module that chooses compact batch shapes (micro, mini, pooled) per-tenant with constraints for P95 latency and minimal throughput impact.
- Quant slab autocalibrator: safe heuristic that prefers lower precision lanes (int8/4) only after simulated smoke-checks against a small eval set (configured per-tenant). Calibration happens off the hot path and records rollback traces.
- CLI: redwood econ refine --dry-run to simulate suggested defaults and export JSON presets for Console.
- Console defaults: UI hooks to preview suggested lane profiles and toggle safe-rollback flags.
- Telemetry: adds metrics: refinery.suggested_lanes, refinery.applied_lanes, refinery.rollback_count and histograms for simulated_loss_delta.
- Tests and bench: unit tests for scoring logic, integration harness with synthetic shape generator, and perf bench results included in commits.

Checklist: 
- [x] Core algorithm and runtime integration
- [x] CLI + Console preview hook
- [x] Metrics + dashboards (telemetry definitions added)
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Simulated smoke checks + rollback paths
- [x] Docs stub in /docs/infra/cost_refinery.md (will be expanded in follow-up)

Changed areas (high level):
- runtime/shard_manager/cost_refinery.go (new): core sampling, scoring, suggestion API
- runtime/batcher/microbatch_slimmer.go (modified): scoring integration and fallback rules
- runtime/quant/auto_calibrator.py (new): small python harness used by integration tests and CLI
- cli/redwood-econ/refine_cmd.go (new): dry-run and apply flow with export flags
- console/defaults/cost_refinery_preview.json (new): UI preview payloads
- telemetry/metrics.yaml (modified): new metric families and dashboards
- helm/charts/redwood/values.yaml (modified): feature flag toggle enabled by default in non-production clusters
- tests/integration/cost_refinery_sim_test.go (new) and tests/perf/refinery_bench.toml (new)
- docs/infra/cost_refinery.md (new)

Commits (summary):
- 9f7a2b: initial cost_refinery service prototype, sampling + scoring
- e3b4c1: integrate microbatch_lanes suggestions into batcher decision path (safe fallback implemented)
- d12f77: quant slab autocalibrator harness + smoke-check runner (python helper)
- 5b9da0: CLI and dry-run exporter implementation (with unit tests)
- 7f4c33: add telemetry metrics and dashboard templates
- ab11e2: integration tests and perf bench artifacts; fix race in sampler
- 2c9980: docs stub and helm toggle; final test fixes

Review conversation (condensed, chronological):
- Marco Diaz (2026-01-20): "Nice direction. Two asks: (1) ensure P95 SLAs are explicitly enforced in the scoring loop (not just as a heuristic), and (2) can we avoid an extra RPC hop in the hot path?"
- Author (Sana) reply: "Added hard constraint check before applying lane suggestions and moved suggestion lookup to a cached local endpoint within shard-manager to avoid cross-shard RPCs. See commit e3b4c1."
- Liam O'Connor (2026-01-22): "Concerned about quant rollouts — need clear observability and an emergency rollback switch. Also request additional unit tests for simulated_loss_delta thresholds."
- Author reply: "Added telemetry for simulated_loss_delta and a config flag `refinery.rollback_on_loss_threshold`. Added unit tests covering threshold edge cases. See tests/integration/cost_refinery_sim_test.go."
- Priya Rao (2026-01-28): "Bench results look promising, but can we gate apply-by-default behind a cluster feature flag for 2 weeks? Also add an admin note to Console with guidance."
- Author reply: "Feature flag added in helm values; Console preview includes admin note stub. We will follow up with rollout runbook (ENG-3321)."
- CI: initial run had intermittent test failure in bench harness (flake) — fixed in ab11e2 by adding deterministic seed and small retry logic. Final CI status: pass.

Risk and mitigation: 
- Risk: quant slab changes could degrade model output quality. Mitigation: autocalibrator performs offline smoke checks and records simulated_loss_delta; any positive degradation above configured threshold is prevented from auto-applying, and the system tags the tenant for manual review.
- Risk: unexpected latency regressions when switching lanes during microbursts. Mitigation: apply uses canary window (default 5 minutes) with rollback on P95 violation and opt-in conservative mode for enterprise tenants.

Release notes (short):
- Introduces Cost Refinery: automated microbatch lane suggestion and safe quant calibration per-tenant. Adds CLI `redwood econ refine` and Console preview. Metrics added for observability. Feature gated via helm flag for staged rollout.

Merge outcome: PR was merged with a squash merge on 2026-02-05 after approvals from Marco and Priya. Commit message: "introduce cost refinery: microbatch lane suggestion + quant autocalibrator (squash)"

Follow-ups (planned):
- ENG-3321: rollout runbook and tenant opt-in UI (follow-up doc + support playbook)
- ENG-3322: extended evaluation harness to run full-model QA on a sample corpus before auto-apply
- DOCS-120: comprehensive docs for operators and tenant admins

Notes for reviewers who want to run locally: 
- Start shard-manager with `--enable-cost-refinery` and run `./cli/redwood-econ/refine --dry-run -o ./out.json`. Perf bench harness available at tests/perf/refinery_bench.toml.

notes: This PR aims to be conservative by default. Feature is behind a helm toggle and requires opt-in to auto-apply in production clusters. Operator docs and runbook will be published as ENG work items linked above.
release_notes: Introduce 'Cost Refinery' to suggest tenant-aware microbatch shapes and safely propose per-tenant quantization slabs. Includes CLI dry-run, Console preview, and observability metrics. Feature gated for staged rollout.
